pr_title: core: split $MONITOR_METADATA and return it only if a single unit triggers OnFailure/OnSuccess
pr_body:
Remove the list logic, and simply skip passing metadata if more than one
unit triggered an OnFailure/OnSuccess handler.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/22370
pr_comments: @bluca @poettering apologies for the extra work this has caused and many thanks for cleaning this up. Let me know if there are any other follow ups I can help with.

> @bluca @poettering apologies for the extra work this has caused and many thanks for cleaning this up. Let me know if there are any other follow ups I can help with.

It's no problem at all, no worries!

This looks much better. But the variable seems weird to me, i.e. why stash that all into one? This should be normalized, separate env vars, so that it's easy for scripts to process. i.e. this is weird:

```
MONITOR_METADATA="SERVICE_RESULT=exit-code,EXIT_CODE=exited,EXIT_STATUS=1,INVOCATION_ID=02dd868af2f344b18edaf74b618b2f90,UNIT=failure.service"
```

should be this instead:

```
MONITOR_SERVICE_RESULT=exit-code
MONITOR_EXIT_CODE=exited
MONITOR_EXIT_STATUS=1
MONITOR_INVOCATION_ID=02dd868af2f344b18edaf74b618b2f90
MONITOR_UNIT=failure.service
```

With that behaviour should be simple and systematic, and very easy to write scripts for.
It's still easy to parse for scripts. It's an attempt to keep backward compatibility intact with v250. But if we prefer to break compatibility, I can change it.

I am pretty sure we should create the normalized environment fields as I suggested. But I'd see that as a separate question from whethre to keep the old MONITOR_METADATA env var too.

I think we should be able to drop it though given that it was not guaranteed to exist anyway (after all, you can start units listed in some other unit's OnFailure=/OnSuccess= lines also directly, in which case the env vars would not exist). i.e. I'd probably just go this way, and drop the old name, document it loudly in NEWS (and maybe highlight in OnFailure=/OnSuccess= that the env vars will only be around if the service is a single other service's OnFailure=/OnSuccess=, and only if that service already exited, and so on, i.e. emphasize the scripts should handle gracefully if the env vars aren't there).

That said, I'd also be OK to keep th old variable in place, but only for compat, i.e. drop it from documentation, and just pass it as one more field, instead of the main conduit for the information.

Mmh while updating the test, I noticed this change in the dependency handling breaks it, and it no longer deterministically associates the OnFailure dependency. Any idea if I am doing the atoms wrong?

> Mmh while updating the test, I noticed this change in the dependency handling breaks it, and it no longer deterministically associates the OnFailure dependency. Any idea if I am doing the atoms wrong?

I've pushed a version that breaks backward compat - but it's borken as above. Not because of the variables, but because of the atoms - sometimes the reference is not present. Any idea what I have forgot?
Hmm, wouldn't it be better to keep the compat variable? The code to generate the text is a self-contained chunk and it shouldn't be a problem to keep it. We can remove it a year or two down the road.

> Hmm, wouldn't it be better to keep the compat variable? The code to generate the text is a self-contained chunk and it shouldn't be a problem to keep it. We can remove it a year or two down the road.

I don't mind one way or another, i thought @poettering was for removal. I don't think anything is using it, codesearch shows nothing. I can leave it if it's the preference.

More importantly right now the atoms handling is borken and need to figure out why
did another review. looks conceptually good to me now, but needs some more polishing i guess.

> did another review. looks conceptually good to me now, but needs some more polishing i guess.

Updated as requested, but it's still borked, and still no idea what I got wrong. Any suggestion?
Thank you so much for the help! Looks great to me

OK, I think this is acceptable and can be merged.

The model where the same cleanup unit is used for multiple service just cannot work too reliably. I thought about enhancing `service_get_triggering_service` to ignore services which haven't failed, but I don't think we can get it to work: we could fix those issues in the testsuite, but it'd introduce wrong behaviour in other cases. In particular, you can have multiple handler services attached to one unit, and they may restart the failed unit, or do reset-failed on it, and we just can't properly keep track of all this if we have a many-to-many mapping. I think it's reasonable to simply push people to use templated cleanup units if they want to watch more than one unit.

issue_context.title: #20833 must be reverted (OnFailure=/OnSuccess= metadata propagation)
issue_context.body:
#20833 contains non-trivial to fix memory corruptions, see my comments there. THis needs some more rounds of review. I would have posted a revert PR, but it already got changed since, hence this issue instead.

This really isn't ready for release, and is a blocker issue hence.
comments:
Follow-ups here: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/22378
For the rest, see comments on #20833
#22378 addressed some of the issues that need fixing, but not all. Hence reopening.

So I think there's some major disconnect in the discussions here. The current implementation focusses on a model where a single service unit processes OnFailure=/OnSuccess= events for a multitude of services. The problems I see all stem from that idea, i.e. the fact that the linked list will trigger a memory corruption in some cases (or that we need the linked list at all), and that events will be lost, if the handler service is already started when another unit requesting it sends out an event too, or that the environment vairable is so hard to process.

The model I always had in mind for this is that each service that shall be monitored this way will get its own private *instance* of a monitoring service. That removes *all* these issues: things become vastly simpler, we don't need linked lists, no complex env vars and events will not get lost anymore.

i.e I think if you have a service foobar.service you want to monitor for failures you'd add a OnFailure=mymonitor@%N.service to it. If you have an instanced service quux@waldo.service you want to monitor you'd instead use OnFailure=mymonitor@%p-%i.service or so.

You then define mymonitor@.service as generic template unit that would get instantiated once for each failure service, and would get passed in the failure data as env var, without any ambiguities or complex way to parse things.

So hence, what's the rationale for the approach that was merged? Can we just rework the way I propose above? To me it appears quite clearly as the safer, cleaner approach.

or to elaborate on this, the usecase I thought this was for was for people who want to hook failing services to an automated email. i.e. with the design I suggested you'd be able to put together a script like this:

```sh
#!/bin/sh

(
    cat <<EOF
I am sorry to report that unit $MONITOR_UNIT on $HOSTNAME failed.

Service Status
--------------
EOF

    systemctl status $MONITOR_UNIT
    cat <<EOF

Execution Environment
---------------------
EOF

    export
) | mail admin@example.com -s "Unit $MONITOR_UNIT on $HOSTNAME failed!"
```

And then, wrap that in a service mymonitor@.service and there you go, you get an email about every failure you OnFailure=-link this template into. This is dead simple. Any approach that tries to multiplex failures from a multitude of services into a single handler service requires much more complex handling...

Do you have a reproducer for the memory corruption issue you mention?

The current implementation will work in both the way you describe (with an instance) and without. It seems a pity to me to remove functionality given it's there, documented, tested, and it works, but if you feel strongly about it, feel free to send a PR to do so.

> Do you have a reproducer for the memory corruption issue you mention?

Adding an item into mltiple linked lists as implemented by the `list.h` macros simply does not work, and is not supported. Hence, reading the code: just define a unit with OnFailure= onto two other units, trigger it, and see how things go south. Because that would mean the Unit object would be linked into two Job objects, right? And Boom!

> The current implementation will work in both the way you describe (with an instance) and without. It seems a pity to me to remove functionality given it's there, documented, tested, and it works, but if you feel strongly about it, feel free to send a PR to do so.

No it does not work. the lists thing doesn't work, and even if you don't trigger use that, then the fact that failure events will be lost if they happen while the monitor service is already started is just buggy behaviour. i.e. if you have both `foo.service` and `bar.service` both have `OnFailure=mymonitor.service`, and then `foo.service` fails and thus causes `mymonitor.service` to be started, which will work, and get the metadata passed in via an env var. Now `mymonitor.service` is a bit slow in what it does, maybe a Python script on an overloaded machine, talking to some external system which is slow. So it takes a couple of seconds to complete. Now, as result of `foo.service` failing `bar.service` also starts to fail. Now this causes `mymonitor.service` to be started – but it already is running! So the start request has no effect and noone will ever take notice of this second service failing, or collect the metadata.

So no, this PR does *not* work. 

And besides that, I wouldn't know how to parse the complex env var in simple shell. I.e. how would go for writing that simple shell script I showed above if you get a bunch of fields all in one for a variety of services.

I can't manage to cause any crashes. The references saved in the list are not modified at all from the list itself, and the atoms ensure they are always around, so the pointers are still valid.

But anyway, it's moot, here's a PR to do the change as requested: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/22460
